body:
My issue is almost an exact replica of https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79234663/c-and-cuda-name-mangling-inconsistent. Quoting the relevant parts here:

> I attempted to compile PyTorch from source but ran into a very strange linking error. After investigating, I discovered that a templated function defined in a C++ file and its declaration in a CUDA file generate two different mangled names.
>
> C++ definition: `_ZNK2at10TensorBase14const_data_ptrIdTnNSt9enable_ifIXntsr3stdE10is_const_vIT_EEiE4typeELi0EEEPKS3_v`
>
> CUDA declaration: `_ZNK2at10TensorBase14const_data_ptrIdTnNSt9enable_ifIXntsr4__T0E10is_const_vIT_EEiE4typeELi0EEEPKS3_v`
>
> The 2 names look almost identical except for the bold parts. When I use llvm-cxxfilt, the 2 mangled names returned the same function name `double const* at::TensorBase::const_data_ptr<double, 0>() const`

My clang version is 18.1.3 and `nvcc --version`
```
nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver
Copyright (c) 2005-2025 NVIDIA Corporation
Built on Tue_May_27_02:21:03_PDT_2025
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86
Build cuda_12.9.r12.9/compiler.36037853_0
```

Going a bit beyond the stack overflow post, I notice 3 different (undefined) mangled symbols in `libtorch_cuda.so` which demangle to the same function name.
```
U _ZNK2at10TensorBase14const_data_ptrIN3c104HalfETnNSt9enable_ifIXntgssr3stdE10is_const_vIT_EEiE4typeELi0EEEPKS5_v
U _ZNK2at10TensorBase14const_data_ptrIN3c104HalfETnNSt9enable_ifIXntsr3stdE10is_const_vIT_EEiE4typeELi0EEEPKS5_v
U _ZNK2at10TensorBase14const_data_ptrIN3c104HalfETnNSt9enable_ifIXntsr4__T0E10is_const_vIT_EEiE4typeELi0EEEPKS5_v
```

One of the commenters in the stack overflow post stated that
> The extra parts in the symbol are typically related to GPU side CUDA ABI attributes

I am currently unable to finish building torch because `libtorch_cpu.so` doesn't produce all the mangled symbols expected by `libtorch_cuda.so`. Any help being able to finish building torch would be incredible

cc @malfet @seemethere @ptrblck @msaroufim @eqy @jerryzh168 @tinglvv @nWEIdia

Which commit did you use to build? I force pushed on that branch a few times. 580851d4ccf71042e1d4e5724471fe58500b97f6 should build fine.

Updating to your newest commit, the only undefined references I see now are 
```
undefined symbol: __atomic_store_8	(./libtorch_cuda.so)
undefined symbol: __atomic_load	(./libtorch_cuda.so)
```
Seems like I might need to try to force `-latomic`. It's interesting that if I do `nm libtorch_cuda.so | grep atomic_load` on a gcc build I don't see any symbols

That's strange, I don't get that error. If I look on Google for this message some stuff comes up but since I am unable to reproduce it locally, I don't think I'll be able to help. Can you share the output of `uname -m` on your machine?

Interesting! I didn't get any link errors at all on `x86_64` even before my PR. If you're interested in digging into it further, here's the setup I use to build PyTorch: https://github.com/lakshayg/pytorch-devel. You can try using this and see if it builds for you.

You'll need to make some changes to the Makefile:

```diff
diff --git a/Makefile b/Makefile
index 0be163a..00f4314 100755
--- a/Makefile
+++ b/Makefile
@@ -38,4 +38,4 @@ edit:

-export CC:=gcc
-export CXX:=g++
+export CC:=clang
+export CXX:=clang++
 export CXXFLAGS:=-Wfatal-errors
@@ -73,3 +73,3 @@ build-%: export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST?=$(shell nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap
 build-%: export BUILD_TEST?=0
-build-%: export BUILD_BINARY?=0
+build-%: export BUILD_BINARY?=1
 build-%: export BUILD_FUNCTORCH?=1
```

Since I have a successful gcc build, I'm probably not going to dig into it too much more. It appears neither libgcc nor libatomic exports those symbols on my system. I don't know why they get injected with clang. Anyway thanks for all the help with the other symbols!

I'm not sure if this is a CUDA vs C++ name mangling problem, but rather a C++17 vs C++20 ABIs problem. I.e. somehow parts of the code are compiled with C++20 symbols manglong, but others with C++17...
